meta.title: Security Event Correlation & MITRE ATT&CK Copilot — PROPOSED MVP DESIGN

views.label: Deterministic security core
views.note: Rules, evidence links, incident state, and ATT&CK mappings are deterministic and testable.

views.label: Grounded AI support
views.note: RAG supplies cited knowledge; the LLM drafts analysis without inventing evidence.

views.label: Learning path
views.note: Read the cards in workflow order to see prerequisites, deferred topics, and required depth.

cards.title: 01 • Security Events — Proposed
items: What this step does: accepts JSON/JSONL authentication, process, and network fixtures.
Input: raw security logs/events.
Output: RawEvent objects.
Security knowledge needed: SOC roles; Event vs Alert vs Incident; SIEM vs EDR; three basic log families and common fields.
Learn before coding: explain Event, Alert, Incident and read one auth, process, and network event.
Can learn later — Future Extension: Splunk, Elastic, EDR APIs, Kafka, advanced Windows Event IDs.
Depth required: Basic working knowledge.
Why this knowledge matters: input facts must be interpreted without turning every event into an alert.

cards.title: 02 • Normalizer — Proposed
items: What this step does: maps source-specific fields into one semantic event contract.
Input: RawEvent objects.
Output: NormalizedEvent objects with stable identifiers, entities, and timestamps.
Security knowledge needed: user/host/IP/process/domain meaning; parent-child processes; source/destination; timeline ordering.
Learn before coding: interpret fields and explain why winword.exe → powershell.exe may matter.
Can learn later — Future Extension: ECS, OCSF, full common-schema compatibility.
Depth required: Basic working knowledge.
Why this knowledge matters: syntactically valid normalization can still destroy security meaning.

cards.title: 03 • Detection Rules — Proposed • Deterministic
items: What this step does: applies explicit thresholds and behavior rules to find suspicious activity.
Input: NormalizedEvent objects.
Output: Detection/Alert with rule ID, evidence, severity, and rationale.
Security knowledge needed: detection engineering; IOC vs behavior/TTP; thresholds; false positives/negatives; brute force and contextual PowerShell/network suspicion.
Learn before coding: tune a simple rule and explain why PowerShell alone is not malicious.
Can learn later — Future Extension: Sigma, YARA, IDS signatures, ML anomaly detection.
Depth required: Basic working knowledge.
Why this knowledge matters: detection asks ‘What is suspicious?’ and must be reproducible—never delegated to the LLM.

cards.title: 04 • Correlation Engine — Proposed • Deterministic Core
items: What this step does: links related detections/events using time, entities, process chains, and shared IOCs.
Input: events plus detections.
Output: correlated evidence group and create/update-incident decision.
Security knowledge needed: event correlation; temporal reasoning; entity/process relationships; evidence; Alert vs Incident.
Learn before coding: justify a score using same user/host/IP/process, time proximity, and shared IOC.
Can learn later — Future Extension: graph databases, attack graphs, probabilistic correlation, ML clustering.
Depth required: Intermediate (start basic, deepen while testing).
Why this knowledge matters: correlation asks ‘Do these suspicious facts belong to one case?’ and is the MVP’s core security logic.

cards.title: 05 • Incident — Proposed • Deterministic
items: What this step does: turns correlated evidence into a durable investigation case and timeline.
Input: related events and detections.
Output: Incident object with status, severity, entities, evidence IDs, and timeline.
Security knowledge needed: lifecycle; triage; severity vs confidence; raw evidence vs finding vs hypothesis.
Learn before coding: explain Candidate/Open/Investigating/Triaged/Resolved/Closed and preserve evidence traceability.
Can learn later — Future Extension: containment, eradication, recovery, formal SOC playbooks.
Depth required: Basic working knowledge.
Why this knowledge matters: Evidence ≠ Hypothesis ≠ Confirmed Fact.

cards.title: 06 • MITRE ATT&CK Mapping — Proposed • Deterministic
items: What this step does: maps observed, evidenced behaviors to explicit ATT&CK technique IDs.
Input: incident detections and observed behaviors.
Output: technique/sub-technique IDs linked back to evidence.
Security knowledge needed: ATT&CK, tactic, technique, sub-technique, TTP, evidence-to-technique mapping.
Learn before coding: distinguish tactic from technique and support T1110/T1059.001 with evidence.
Can learn later — Future Extension: broad matrix coverage and automated ATT&CK content updates; do not memorize the matrix.
Depth required: Beginner to Basic working knowledge.
Why this knowledge matters: deterministic mapping prevents unsupported LLM guesses from becoming security facts.

cards.title: 07 • Security RAG — Proposed • AI Support
items: What this step does: retrieves relevant, versioned ATT&CK/security guidance with source metadata.
Input: incident, technique IDs, keywords, and entities.
Output: relevant cited chunks.
Security knowledge needed: reading ATT&CK descriptions; investigation guidance; trusted sources; citation traceability.
Learn before coding: judge whether a source supports an investigation claim; reuse existing chunking/search/reranking skills.
Can learn later — Future Extension: hybrid retrieval, advanced reranking, larger security corpora.
Depth required: Security Beginner; RAG uses existing AI skills.
Why this knowledge matters: RAG supplies knowledge—it does not replace detection or correlation.

cards.title: 08 • LLM Investigation Copilot — Proposed • AI Support
items: What this step does: synthesizes evidence, timeline, ATT&CK mappings, and retrieved context into a structured draft.
Input: incident, evidence, timeline, mappings, and cited chunks.
Output: summary, severity explanation, evidence, hypotheses, next steps, confidence, and citations.
Security knowledge needed: SOC investigation questions; evidence vs hypothesis; timeline; IOC/TTP use; basic investigation workflow.
Learn before coding: ask what/when/who/where/evidence/next and label uncertainty explicitly.
Can learn later — Future Extension: multi-agent SOC and automated remediation.
Depth required: Security Basic; reuse structured-output, validation, retry, fallback, HITL, and evaluation skills.
Why this knowledge matters: the LLM must not invent events, IOCs, techniques, or unsupported root cause.

cards.title: 09 • Investigation Report — Proposed
items: What this step does: presents an analyst-friendly, reviewable investigation artifact.
Input: validated structured copilot output plus traceable source/evidence references.
Output: incident summary, severity, timeline, key evidence, techniques, hypotheses, next steps, and citations.
Security knowledge needed: analyst report structure; evidence traceability; fact vs hypothesis; severity explanation.
Learn before coding: write a short report where every factual claim links to evidence or a cited source.
Can learn later — Future Extension: SOC case-system export and formal report templates.
Depth required: Beginner.
Why this knowledge matters: analysts need auditable facts and clearly bounded hypotheses, not fluent unsupported prose.
